bugs.text: bez(p,t) reads p[0][0], p[1][0]... (array of points) but every path built in the game is an object {p0,p1,p2,p3}. The first enemy entry update at 526 throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 0)' on the first frame of play, before render(); the throw repeats every frame (18,062 errors in the play-test). The screen freezes on the first play frame, the player is never seen (hidden by the invulnerability blink on that frame), no enemy ever appears, and nothing can be done except P (which only hides the error). The same mismatch would crash every dive, return and beam approach.
Stage badges show up to three flags labelled by stage number via vals[st-1] (stage 2 shows '1' and '5' flags) instead of decomposing the stage into 50/30/20/10/5/1 badges.

Challenge wave bonus: waves not yet spawned have no live enemies and are marked resolved with 0 kills on the first frame, so the 1,000 wave bonus can only ever be awarded for wave 0 (unreachable in practice).
Dead code: challengeWaveDone is a self-labelled placeholder that is never called; hitBox returns a comma expression and is unused; line 746 filters with a condition that is always true.

Entry stagger is done by a negative bezier parameter (t=-i*0.18); bez extrapolates for t<0 so staggered enemies would start far outside the path's start point rather than waiting (latent; unreachable).
Canvas is only centred horizontally (block + margin:auto); not vertically centred on the page.

summary: The file is tidy and reads like a plan for a faithful Galaga: pixel-art sprites for the three enemy types with wing frames, a bezier entry/dive system in staggered groups, boss escorts with 400/800/1600 scoring, a widening tractor beam with capture, rescue, docking and a hostile captive, challenging stages with wave and perfect bonuses, seven synthesized sounds, a fixed-timestep loop and a correct title screen and HUD. None of it is ever exercised: the bezier helper takes an array of points while every path is built as an object, so the first frame of play throws a TypeError, render stops, and the screen stays frozen on an empty playfield with no player and no enemies. Beyond that single fatal mismatch the code has leftover stubs, a wrong stage-badge rule and a broken wave-bonus bookkeeping, but as delivered it is a title screen followed by a freeze.
